verdict.rationale: Kimi documents an official terminal CLI, Kimi Code CLI. Users launch it with `kimi` and sign in with `/login`. It can read code, edit files, run commands, search the web, and complete development tasks autonomously, and other editors can connect to it via ACP. A probe confirms the docs serve and that the CLI is bundled with Kimi Membership, and one community user reports the Kimi CLI outperforms OpenCode for Kimi models. Missing for 10: in-depth command/flag reference documentation and broader independent hands-on corroboration of the CLI.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can use an official CLI

citations.quote: Chat with AI in the terminal, letting it read code, edit files, execute commands, search the web, and autonomously complete development tasks.
run `kimi` in the terminal to start; on first use, log in to the Kimi Code platform with the `/login` command to complete the connection
Other editors such as JetBrains and Zed can connect via CLI's ACP protocol.
